differences: The paper says the four participants left out made no recorded movements; in the shared rows 3 of the four have no cursor movement and 1 has cursor movement on some trials (they are the four the authors' script skips, so they are flagged subject_excluded_by_authors).
calibration success, mean (%): the paper reports 72, the shared rows give 72.99 (Methods, calibration, Methods and Results (bioRxiv 2023.07.19.549705)).
65% group: t against the intended 35% success: the paper reports 3.03, the shared rows give 7.735 (Results, error-rate control, Methods and Results (bioRxiv 2023.07.19.549705)).
65% group: p of that t: the paper reports 0.004, the shared rows give 5.555e-10 (Results, error-rate control, Methods and Results (bioRxiv 2023.07.19.549705)).

The paper's ten learning-index outliers (1.75 IQR rule on a precision measure built from the trial errors) are not flagged: the first batch does not log the trial error, so the measure cannot be rebuilt from the shared rows.

In the first batch (all_subjects_fast.json) endpoint_y is a placeholder (mostly 0) and the authors' script rebuilds the error from the puck's launch values and the last cursor sample; outcome_error is therefore filled for the second batch only, where endpoint_y is the final puck minus paddle-centre distance the script uses.
The last 10 trials of each participant (attempt 100-109, fixed difficulty) are shared but the authors' script does not use them; they are marked excluded_by_authors.
